contract.note: Reading linear scaling as roughly proportional is ordinary. Making the test adjust for the discounts follows the speaker's own framing. The counterfactual for 'only reason' is fair. Which costs count, and how a ramp-up differs from a discount, still decide the result.

evidence.note: Company S-1, available before the cutoff. Implied adjusted cost ratio drops from about 113% in Q1 to about 81% in Q2, but the figures are not adjusted for the May–June fee cuts. Company disclosure; it cannot isolate the discount effect.
Reports an unspecified reduced SpaceX fee for May–June before the $1.25B/month rate. Shows different starting terms but gives no savings amount or capacity-matched comparison.

reviews.rationale: The falling raw cost ratio does not settle either half of the claim. The contract tests scaling after removing the discounts, and tests 'only reason' with a counterfactual using normal fees. The packet has neither the discount amounts nor matching capacity data, so neither test can be run. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The draft keeps the universal scope ('every app', 'every AI company'), the exclusive cause and the price tiers. It is a firm causal assertion, not hedged.

contract.note: Treating the prices as examples and the universal causal claim as open to a single counterexample is an ordinary reading of firm language. The speaker named venture capital as the cause, so a provider with no VC money is a fair test.

evidence.note: Dated March 2026 report (relaying The Information) that Midjourney is profitable, bootstrapped, has no outside investors, and runs its own model with paid subscriptions. The profitability figures come from the CEO, but the report is clearly sourced.

reviews.rationale: The claim says every AI company can sell subscriptions only because VC subsidizes the industry. Midjourney, a profitable model provider with no outside investors selling paid subscriptions in Q1 2026, is a documented counterexample, which meets the contract's contradiction condition. Some supplier concessions cannot be ruled out, but the speaker named venture capital, not suppliers.
